case_payload.fixed_engineering_facts: Source-derived scenario (Table A4, PDF page 14): frequency C, severity I, Low risk. No consequence or existing safeguard is listed for high flow. The source recommends checking and confirming the control-room high-flow alarm referred to as PIT-101. The published tag is retained without assuming a corrected instrument identity. Synthetic decision-model assumptions: the fixed cost is in arbitrary normalized units, not a source-derived price. The stated reliability is experimentally stipulated, not a source-derived performance estimate. The verification proposal concerns the source-listed alarm function; no additional hazardous consequence is assigned to high flow. A demand means a high-flow alarm demand after the proposed verification work. Success means delivery of the intended high-flow indication in the control room. There are exactly two mutually exclusive and exhaustive outcomes per demand: successful delivery of this specified function, or unavailability of this function. For this exercise, unavailability means that the specified function is not successfully delivered on demand, including failure to perform it; this is an operational definition, not a general equivalence of reliability and availability. The decision concerns the next 100 eligible demands after the proposed action is in place; their occurrence rate is not specified. Reliability applies only to this function and does not quantify accident prevention or elimination of residual risk.
case_payload.proposal: Verify the control-room high-flow alarm referred to as PIT-101 in Table A4 and confirm that its intended alarm function is active.
case_payload.title: Verification of the source-listed high-flow alarm

condition_payload.manipulation_text: Reliability assessment: the specified function will be delivered successfully on 95 of 100 demands and will be unavailable on 5 of 100 demands.

surface_form_payload.question_text: Should management reject this safeguard recommendation?

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: The proposed safeguard carries out the explicit recommendation recorded in the source HAZOP (Table A4) to verify that the control-room alarm referred to as PIT-101 is active. At an experimentally stipulated delivery success rate of 95 percent (5 percent unavailability) and an implementation cost of 20.0 normalized units, executing this verification is a cost-effective operational integrity check. Although baseline risk is Low (frequency C, severity I) with no consequence listed, confirming alarm availability supports design intent monitoring and resolves tag ambiguity. Consequently, management should approve the recommendation rather than reject it.

supporting_evidence.relevance: Establishes baseline Low risk (frequency C, severity I), notes absence of listed consequences, documents source recommendation to verify PIT-101, and defines the demand framework.
Identifies the reference scenario deviation as more flow in separator vessel V-001 and outlet lines.
Specifies the node under review as V-001 and associated lines.

uncertainty_notes: The instrument tag PIT-101 standardly denotes pressure indication rather than flow, creating ambiguity regarding instrument functionality.
No specific hazardous consequence or existing safeguard is listed in Table A4 for the high-flow deviation.
Demand frequency and occurrence rate for high-flow events are not specified.
Stipulated reliability applies solely to alarm function delivery and does not quantify accident prevention or residual risk reduction.
